system:
You draft public Twitter replies for Spotify's customer support account (@SpotifyCares), in 2017.

You will be given a customer's message and a numbered list of PRECEDENTS: real past customer messages with the reply Spotify actually sent. Your reply must be consistent with those precedents.

Hard rules:
- Ground every factual claim in the precedents. If the precedents do not establish something, do not say it.
- Never invent a policy, price, timeframe, refund, or entitlement.
- Never promise an action Spotify would have to take on the customer's account (refunding, resetting, unlocking, cancelling). You cannot see their account.
- If the precedents mainly ask the customer for more information, then asking for that same information IS the correct reply.
- Match the register of the precedents: warm, brief, lower-case-friendly, first person plural. Under 280 characters.
- If the precedents do not actually address the customer's problem, say so honestly in the `reply` and give a low confidence.

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"reply": "<the reply text>", "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "evidence_ids": ["<ids you used>"]}

`confidence` is how well the precedents support your reply, not how fluent it is.
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
a while ago you guys made repeat 1 disable after switching songs. While I understand this may be good for some people it's terribly impractical for people who switch songs through bluetooth and want to keep repeat 1 on. Any chance you guys could make it toggleable?

PREDICTED INTENT: other

PRECEDENTS:

[249054] (similarity 0.69, intent other)
  past customer: did you remove the functionality to put one song on repeat?
  spotify replied: Hey Michael! Can you let us know what device you're using Spotify on? We'll see what we can suggest

[2565920] (similarity 0.57, intent other)
  past customer: Why does Spotify insist on enabling repeat constantly? I listen to albums, and NEVER want repeat enabled. When I'm done an album, I move onto another. ?
  spotify replied: Hey Matt! Don't worry, we can help. Can you let us know the device/OS you're using? We'll see what we can suggest

[2422819] (similarity 0.55, intent other)
  past customer: why do radio stations of songs only have a set number of songs before they start repeating? Such a good possible option that only seems to go halfway.
  spotify replied: Thanks for the info and feedback. These will be passed on to the relevant folks. Let us know if there's anything else we can help with

[2030602] (similarity 0.52, intent other)
  past customer: Dear devs, pls give us a "listen to same thing at same time feature"! Like my own radio. Or a "play same" button. Down to the ms!
  spotify replied: Hey! Thanks for the idea. We'll be sure to let our team know it's something you'd like to see

[2595615] (similarity 0.52, intent other)
  past customer: can you give the option to scroll through the Popular songs? Switching from Napster and I liked this feature. <link>
  spotify replied: Hi Angela! We don't have any info on this right now, but we'll let the right team know it's something you'd like to see

Draft the reply as JSON.
